doc.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Venues, circuits and the music business
title: Big bands, dancing and the concert hall
summary: People now listen rather than dance, and she says that is not why the music is poorly presented.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: How about the relationship between the big bands and dance? What do you think of the way the bands in the '40s, particularly, the popular dance music, and it was a venue where that could happen?
Is part of the reason that it hasn't moved into the concert hall maybe because it was connected with a space where people could -­

People don't dance to this music anymore. They listen. When Charlie Parker and Max Roach and that crowd came, it wasn't -- well, some people -- you know, they used to jitterbug. We used to jitterbug. You can dance to anything. If you're in concert, though, you don't want people dancing. You want the attention of the audience
